correctness.rationale: Rechecked the 16 physical Walsh sign patterns: epsilon_0=1, epsilon_5=epsilon_1 epsilon_2 epsilon_3 epsilon_4. Including each overall negative yields all 32 even-parity patterns and leaves absolute even moments unchanged. Every sign monomial of degree ≤4 orthogonal to constants has mean zero on this parity subgroup, giving E|Σepsilon_j z_j|²=6 and fourth moment 60+|Σz_j²|²≥60. With sixth roots z_j in Z[zeta], each squared sample is an Eisenstein norm a²+ab+b², and the only attainable nonnegative values below 12 are 0,1,3,4,7,9. If the peak were less than 12 then Y²≤9Y would force fourth moment ≤54, contradiction. Explicit coefficients z_j=zeta^j give physical square magnitudes 0×4,4×6,12×6. Independently wrote an exact-integer full 6^5=7776 normalized-tuple enumeration using the norm form, obtaining exactly 480 sharp tuples and complete histogram [(12,480),(13,320),(16,976),(19,2400),(21,2112),(25,480),(27,320),(28,480),(31,192),(36,16)]. This is genuinely exhaustive for the stated discrete alphabet, not a numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: Six-phase alphabet is standard for polyphase signal synthesis and the six-character affine circuit is the minimal natural six-character Boolean dependency used here, forcing a parity-restricted rather than arbitrary sign design. A full sharp peak/PAPR and complete finite optimal-design count is a motivated spectral invariant with a rigorous fourth-moment/Eisenstein gap explanation plus exact exhaustive classification. final_claim: For six Walsh characters forming an affine circuit in F_2^4 and coefficients restricted to sixth roots of unity, the exact minimum squared peak over 16 physical samples is 12 (PAPR 2), and exactly 480 coefficient tuples modulo common sixth-root rotation attain it.
